- An excerpt of your Article 30 processing ledger covering the last 6 months (high level is fine; we may request a redacted example).
- A current inventory of subprocessors with country and purpose (we need to confirm onshore vs cross-border handling).
- Retention mapping for account-related telemetry and request logs (how long each bucket is retained and where).
- A short description of the chain-of-custody for audit exports (who has access to export logs; are exports wrapped with KMS?).

We are aiming to present this to internal legal on Friday 6/18. Can you confirm what you can share by 6/15 and whether a technical walkthrough to show log extraction is possible the week of 6/22?

If there are constraints (on-prem proof needs extra paperwork, or SOC artifacts aren't sharable), flag them up and we'll work with procurement.

- Article 30 ledger excerpt: we can provide an export that lists processing activities, categories of data, and subprocessors for the period you requested. We will redact customer identifiers by default; happy to produce a tighter redaction for your internal legal team.
- Subprocessor inventory: attached (subprocessor_inventory_v2.csv) — includes country and declared purpose. Note: a few vendors are in transition; I'll call those out in a follow-up note.
- Retention mapping: attached (retention_matrix.xlsx). It includes telemetry buckets and retention periods; there are two buckets where retention is configurable per-account (we can lock these if required under the DPA).
- Chain-of-custody for exports: we use KMS-wrapped export keys and RBAC-based export workflows. Access is limited to an internal roles group; exports are logged and signed. Irene will reply with the exact log fields we can provide as a sample.
- Sample access log: see action item to provide a redacted snippet (Irene).

Timeline: we can hand over the attached CSV/XLSX by EOD today. For the technical walkthrough, proposed slots the week of 6/22: Tue 6/23 10:00-11:00 PT, Wed 6/24 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works best for your ops team?

Best,

Hi Sally — following up with the technical details Markus promised. I've pulled a short, redacted Art.30 ledger excerpt and a log snippet as examples (attached). Notes below: 

1) Art.30 ledger export (art30_ledger_excerpt.txt): includes processing activity id, purpose, categories of data processed, subprocessors involved, and the legal basis recorded. We redact account identifiers and IPs by default; if you need less redaction for an inspection, we'll need a signed NDA/amendment to the DPA for inspector access.

2) Access log snippet (kv_cache_access_log_snippet.log): this is a 10-line redacted sample showing timestamps, operation (EXPORT/READ), actor role, and export request id. We remove request payloads. Full export logs include an HMAC and KMS-wrapping metadata.

3) KMS & chain-of-custody: exports are encrypted via our KMS (customer-wrapped keys available for Private deployments). Export artifacts are staged in a temporary bucket with time-limited URLs and are accessible only to users in the "security-exports" role. All actions are recorded in the audit ledger. Attached is a short SOC stub (Redwood_SOC2_A2025.pdf) summarizing control coverage; we can route the full SOC package under an NDA.

4) Retention snapshots: retention_matrix.xlsx includes both default retention and configurable fields. If Pioneer requires onshore-only retention for specific buckets, we can map those to dedicated retention profiles (requires an onboarding flag).

5) Action items (from our side):
- Deliver redacted Art.30 excerpt (attached).
- Deliver redacted access-log sample (attached).
- Schedule technical walkthrough (Markus to coordinate).
- Confirm whether Pioneer legal needs inspector-level exceptions (if yes, we will prepare a limited-access playbook).

If you want, I can run the extraction live during the walkthrough so your auditor can see the exact fields. Proposed times from Markus look fine; I can host the technical demo.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
